gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 diagnoses failure of a finite-collocation multiplicative quadrature equivalence caused by residual evaluation kernels. It does not identify the distinct coefficient normalization and resulting N-dependent regularization factor in the Monte Carlo finite-feature objective.

Both concern the empirical optimization problem, but ISSUE-002 identifies finite-evaluation degeneracy invalidating a multiplicative loss comparison. It does not recognize the missing nonnegativity/sign hypothesis needed to prevent the objective from being unbounded below and to establish minimizer existence.

ISSUE-002 attacks a relative loss equivalence using nonzero functions in the finite-evaluation kernel. It does not diagnose the incompatibility of setwise convergence with finite atomic quadrature measures converging to an atomless measure, nor does its additive-error repair recognize that specific convergence-assumption defect.

Both identify that finite point evaluations have a nontrivial kernel in the infinite-dimensional space, allowing empirical loss zero while continuous loss is positive and thereby falsifying the claimed uniform multiplicative equivalence. Both also identify replacement by a uniform additive quadrature estimate as the repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The finite-collocation loss cannot uniformly control the continuous loss multiplicatively over the full RKBS norm ball because residuals can vanish at all sampled points while remaining nonzero elsewhere; the associated finite-K error argument therefore requires an additive quadrature estimate instead.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed relative/multiplicative continuous-versus-empirical loss bound fails because finite collocation has a nontrivial evaluation kernel, and the dependent error theorem must instead use a uniform additive quadrature estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 independently diagnoses the finite-evaluation kernel counterexample, the failure of the two-sided multiplicative equivalence, its impact on the finite-K error guarantee, and the additive-error replacement.
